name: Potiphera
overview: Potiphera is a male figure identified in Scripture as the priest of On, also known as Heliopolis. His role as a priest highlights his religious standing in ancient Egypt. Beyond this unique attribute, there is limited additional information about his tribe or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Potiphera' is presented as a proper name without an explicit meaning given. He is also referred to by the title 'priest of On,' which identifies his religious office connected to the city of On (Heliopolis). These titles underscore his priestly role rather than conveying a specific meaning from the Hebrew or Greek.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Potiphera as the father of Asenath, establishing a familial link that connects him to the broader biblical narrative. No other family relationships are noted beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Potiphera's significance in the biblical account centers on his position as a priest of On and his relationship to Asenath, who becomes intertwined with the story of Joseph. His priestly office situates him within the religious landscape of Egypt, providing context to Joseph's marriage and integration into Egyptian society. Thus, Potiphera serves as a key figure linking Joseph to Egyptian culture and faith practices.
